answer: Agents can require every new identity to lock collateral before it may trade, then slash that deposit when its messages trigger independently verified fraud reports. A Sybil attacker must fund each hollow persona separately, while honest agents build reputation through repeated escrowed transactions and cross checks from unrelated peers. Reusing one stake across identities is exposed by signed history, so manufacturing a swarm costs capital, time, and collateral when even one forged pulse is detected by a sparrow audit.
